name: Turn meeting notes into action items and a follow-up email with OpenAI

parameters.content:
## Try me out!

### Turn meeting notes into action items with OpenAI

Paste a meeting transcript (or a few messy bullets) and this workflow returns a clean debrief: a short summary, the decisions that were actually made, a table of **action items with an owner and due date**, and a ready-to-send follow-up email — plus a count of open action items you can branch on later.

Unlike a plain "summarize this" prompt, the model is asked for **structured JSON**, and a Code node parses it safely: if the reply is not valid JSON, the workflow still returns the prose instead of crashing. The prompt also forbids inventing facts — anything not in the notes is written as `not stated`.

### Setup
1. Add your OpenAI credentials to the *Summarize Meeting with OpenAI* node. GPT-4o-mini is cheap (well under $0.01 per meeting).
2. Open *Set Meeting Notes and Attendees* and replace `meeting_title`, `attendees`, `tone` and `raw_notes` with your own meeting. `raw_notes` accepts a full transcript, a pasted chat log, or messy bullets.
3. Click **Test workflow**. The finished debrief appears in *Set Meeting Summary* as `meeting_summary`, `follow_up_email` and `action_item_count`.

### Customize
- Change the model in the OpenAI node (GPT-4o, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for better extraction on long transcripts.
- Swap the final *Set Meeting Summary* node for Slack, Gmail or Notion to deliver the debrief automatically.
- Feed `action_item_count` into an IF node to escalate meetings that produced too many open items.

MIT-licensed and free. Part of a free, open-source n8n workflow library with more ready-to-import templates: https://github.com/zhp910318/n8n-ai-automation-lab

## 1. Trigger and input

A **manual trigger** starts the run. *Set Meeting Notes and Attendees* holds the `meeting_title`, `attendees`, `tone` and `raw_notes` that drive everything downstream. Edit these fields to debrief any meeting — no other node needs changing.

## 2. Extract a structured debrief

*Summarize Meeting with OpenAI* sends the notes to GPT-4o-mini and asks for **strict JSON** (summary, decisions, action items with owner + due date, follow-up email). The system prompt forbids inventing facts: anything absent from the notes comes back as `not stated`.

## 3. Parse safely and output

*Parse Meeting Debrief* strips code fences, `JSON.parse`s the reply and falls back to prose if the model returns invalid JSON, so the workflow never hard-fails on a bad completion. It also builds a Markdown table and counts open action items. *Set Meeting Summary* exposes `meeting_summary`, `follow_up_email` and `action_item_count` for the next node.

assignments.name: raw_notes
assignments.value: PASTE YOUR MEETING TRANSCRIPT OR NOTES HERE. Example: Ana asked if we can import her old spreadsheet before Friday. Sam said the importer handles CSV but not XLSX yet, so we need a quick conversion step. We agreed to ship CSV import this week and revisit XLSX next sprint. Ana will send the export by Wednesday. Sam will document the conversion step.

values.content: You turn messy meeting notes into a structured debrief. Only use information present in the notes. If something is unknown, write "not stated" instead of guessing. Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else - no prose, no code fences.
